name: Kitten Forest
lore: Past the Goblin King's throne the road runs on into a lantern-lit wood of giant toadstools, where kittens nap, play and make mischief in every glade.
sourceNote: FLUX.1 [schnell] by Black Forest Labs (Apache-2.0), 4-bit GGUF, run on the studio's Mac; 103 candidates, 50 picks and 27 spares (game-research/sappers-path-v4/lands/01-kitten-forest/README.md). Each picture's file is the subject-cropped 160 px source with its fixed chroma (that README's hand-off warning), so convert gives back exactly the boards the picks were judged on.

profile.note: Land 1, casual (Peter's direction change, 2026-10-06, mid fix pass: the picture lands become a relaxed Zen mode open from the start, and difficulty climbs in the 200-level castle campaign instead; tools/land-01-notes.md §10). Tags E18/N26/H6/X0: pairs of Normals with an Easy breather after each, a lone Hard every 7-10 levels (land-plan landTags spreads a casual land's few Hards evenly), ending on a Hard at 250. Light features: ? cards (2-3) on a fifth of the Easy, half the Normal and every Hard level; linked squads (1-2 pairs) on a fifth, two fifths and two thirds; mystery blocks on 3 in 10 Normals and half the Hards (of 0.25-0.40 of the eligible blocks off the subject's face); no locks. Generous random-tap bands (Easy 45-80%, Normal 20-50%, Hard 6-20%), no lookahead or careful-player ceilings (both are still graded per level). Every invariant holds, and the steady 1 s replay must win with no wait over 15 s between taps (the critics' m2, m3). The 50 pictures: the set after the visual critic's swaps, laid out again for these tags (few-colour boards on the Easy levels, the busiest on the Hards; no neighbours sharing a category, ground colour family or coat; no orange cat within two of another; near-repeat ideas 10+ apart).
